# Twitter / X — 2026

**The account comes back, and it comes back as an AI user.** 26 posts, and the
year documents something no other page in this directory does: Dan operating
autonomous software agents, building tools against his own data, and using a
model to reconfigure the recommendation systems that shape what he sees.

It is also the year music production resumes under a new name.

## MOGZART, 4 March

> *"'Odd Mob - Never Alone (feat Lizzy Land) [MOGZART DnB JUMP UP REMIX]' is on
> #SoundCloud"*

The first original music released on this account since the SLOPPP micromix
re-post of March 2015 — eleven years — and it is under a different alias, in a
different genre. `wiki/interests/music/overview` records MOGZART and GRIPNOTIC
as successors to SLOPPP; this dates a MOGZART release precisely, and the
2 June post (*"there is just stupid amounts of great DnB coming out right
now"*) places the genre commitment as current rather than incidental.

## The agents

- **5 April**: *"I'm claiming my AI agent 'resourcefulbot' on @moltbook"*
- **7 April**: *"I'm claiming my AI agent 'gripnotic' on @moltbook"*

Two named autonomous agents, one of them carrying the name of a music project.

- **30 May**: *"claude in chrome is sick. i just wiped out all of my follows on here, YT and soundcloud and can rebuild my algo and timelines proper now."*

That is the most interesting sentence on the page. He uses a browser agent to
**delete every follow across three platforms at once**, explicitly in order to
rebuild the recommendation systems from scratch. `wiki/mind/synthesis/millennial-digital-witness`
describes a disposition for watching the medium rather than the event; here the
disposition becomes an **operation**. He is not observing the algorithm. He is
taking an instrument to it, on himself, deliberately.

- **13 June**: *"Man I thought I was being nuts running fable5 for like 14 hours to build this new website and data visualizers of my text logs but who's the crazy one now huh?"*

Fourteen unbroken hours of model-assisted work, building visualisers over his
own message archive. That is this project — or a sibling of it — described from
the inside, on a public feed, by the person doing it.

- **13 June**, on guardrails, in two posts: irritation that xAI had blocked Grok from installing cracked software, on the same day a permissive Claude configuration was withdrawn. His stated use was mundane (*"i was only using it to install some VST/AU plugins for Ableton"*), and the complaint is about capability being removed rather than about the task.
- **14 June**: *"I know a lot of people who would usually be super early adopters who just haven't done anything beyond writing their work emails. There's a large contingent of people who have yet to fully grasp the real utility yet."*

## The agent that ran away, 31 May

> *"okay i woke up to find that the app i built with the new Grok CLI coding
> agent to auto-respond on iMessage for specific numbers had just spent about 5
> hours mass-spam texting garbled unicode to my ex girlfriend."*
> *"so it actually outperformed what i had asked it to build. sick."*

An autonomous messaging agent, built overnight, that ran unsupervised for
roughly five hours and sent a stream of corrupted text to a private contact.
**The recipient is not identified here and no account is built from it** — the
finding is the software failure and the response to it.

And the response is the finding. There is no alarm, no apology and no mention
of consequences: the outcome is reported as an *overperformance*. A tool given
an objective, left unsupervised, that exceeded its instruction in a way that
reached a real person — filed as a joke, in public, the same morning. It is the
clearest illustration in the corpus of the gap `CONTEXT_CORE_EXPANDED` names as
the standing failure mode: **the diagnosis is not missing and the behaviour does
not follow from it.** He is precise about what the agent did and entirely
uninterested in what it means that it did it.

## Politics, in the year's own vocabulary

Three posts on 2 June: *"EVERYBODY🙏"* / *"HATES🙏"* / *"ISRAEL🙏"*. On
29 August, Curtis Sliwa assessed for his *"antizionist credentials"* and a
possible *"Tucker lane of nat con populists"*; a Conner O'Malley bit about
*"Irish Zionism"*; and on 7 August and 1 September, admiration for Abdul
El-Sayed's *"adversarial tv hits"*.

This is the material `skills/corpus/vocabulary-drift.md` was written about — a
political keyword pattern built from 2012–2024 language reported 2026 as
**0.0% political**, when it is roughly a quarter. The vocabulary moved and the
instrument did not.

Also 29 August, on a viral clip: *"There's a big difference between 'you're
going to want to turn around and get out of here' and 'turn around and get out
of here'"* — vertical authority detected at the granularity of a modal verb.

## Texture

On 29 August, over a DHS post about an ICE arrest of Milo Yiannopoulos:
*"My only child's namesake."* His dog is named Milo. And the 30 May run —
*"marinara."* / *"on the wall."* / *"who's the baddest of them all?"* — which is
the 2013 register arriving intact in 2026.

## What would change this reading

This is the live year and the page is a snapshot: 26 posts to 1 September, and
the reading of 2026 as "the AI year" is drawn from about eight of them. The
agent incident is interpreted here as an absence of alarm; an equally available
reading is that alarm existed and was not posted, which is exactly what the 2015
and 2025 blackouts show this account does with difficult material. The
distinction matters and this page cannot settle it.
